hooks.name: typecheck on source save
hooks.description: Runs tsc --noEmit whenever a TypeScript or CSS file is saved. Strict mode is on, and a single unused import fails the build, so the window between 'it compiles' and 'it does not' must be zero.

hooks.name: costume parity on scene save
hooks.description: Runs scripts/parity.ts whenever a scene file is saved. This is the only automated defence of the project's central claim — that both costumes perform the identical beat graph — so it must fire before the change can be believed, not at the end of the session.

hooks.name: stage contract review on source save
hooks.description: Asks the agent to re-check a saved stage file against the cue contract: no second data source, no visual derived from a beat id, no cue read in a component to decide layout.

action.prompt:
A stage file was just saved. Check it against the cue contract in .kiro/steering/cue-contract.md and report only real violations:

1. Does this file write any --cue-* custom property? Only src/hooks/useCueStage.ts may write them. Components must read.
2. Does any visual decision in this file depend on a beat id, a scene id, or a costume name rather than on a --cue-* value or a costume token? `[data-costume='vhs']` overrides for structural differences (drop cap, letterpress) are allowed; branching on costume to pick a different layout is not.
3. Is there a second source of truth for a value the stage already exposes? CueConsole must read the DOM, not React props.
4. Are units and ranges still inside the contract (0..1 meters, focus -1..1, a mood the palette knows)?

If nothing is wrong, say so in one line and stop. Do not refactor proactively. Do not restate the contract back to me.

hooks.name: session orientation
hooks.description: Puts the one-paragraph framing and the verification commands at the top of every session so a fresh agent does not start by re-deriving what GHOSTLIGHT is.

action.command: echo 'GHOSTLIGHT — an interactive haunting where the stage is the interface. Two costumes (seance / vhs), one 17-beat graph, three endings each. The story hands the stage a StageCue; useCueStage eases it into CSS custom properties; every visual derives from them. Read .kiro/steering/cue-contract.md before changing anything under src/styles or src/hooks. Gates: bun run typecheck · bun run parity · bun run build. Never add a second source of truth for a cue value.'

hooks.name: ship gate on agent stop
hooks.description: Before the agent declares work finished, the three gates run. A costume that has drifted or a build that does not compile must be reported, not announced as done.

action.command: bun run typecheck && bun run scripts/parity.ts && bun run build
